title: Macterm project
description: A Macterm project declaration. One file for each project in ~/.config/macterm/projects/. It declares the path of the project and, if you want, its tab and pane layout. Macterm matches a file to a project by `path`. The file name does not matter. "Save Layout" writes the file. You can edit it by hand.

name.description: The display name that Macterm recorded when it saved the file. The project list of the app keeps its own name while the app runs, so the two names can be different. This name is only information.

path.description: Where the project lives, in the scp style. An absolute path, or a path that starts with ~, is a local directory (for example "~/dev/api"). The reserved literal "<pinned>" marks this file as the pinned-tabs layout (pinned.yaml), which Macterm keeps up to date by itself. "[user@]host:dir" is a directory on a remote host (for example "devbox:~/dev/api"). The host can be an ssh-config alias. Port and identity come from ~/.ssh/config. ControlMaster there makes splits fast. This value is the identity of the project: Macterm matches files to projects by this value. The match expands ~ and normalizes ./.. segments. It does not resolve symlinks (including /tmp → /private/tmp), and it does not resolve letter case. Write the directory exactly as the file system reports it. Remote paths match by structure (same user, host and directory). The panes of a remote project run persistent zmx sessions on the host over ssh. zmx must be installed there.

zmxPath.description: The absolute path to zmx on the remote host. Macterm uses it as written, in place of resolving `zmx` through PATH. It applies only to a remote `path`. Set it when the pane shows "zmx not found in PATH". Non-interactive ssh gets a bare PATH. On some hosts, Macterm cannot resolve zmx by itself: a host with a network-mounted home, a host with an unusual /bin/sh, and a host whose PATH is set only in a non-POSIX shell. Example: "~/bin/zmx" or "/usr/local/bin/zmx". Leave it out to find zmx in PATH.

tabs.description: The tabs to create, in order. Leave it out for a bare declaration (nothing to apply).

tab.description: A tab: a layout node (a leaf pane or a split) with an optional `name`. There is no `layout:` wrapper. The fields of the node are at the tab level.

node.description: A node in the split tree. It is a leaf pane (cwd, run and shell) or a split (a `split` mapping). A bare {} is a plain shell pane.

name.description: The title of the tab. When you apply the layout, Macterm matches live tabs by this name.

cwd.description: The working directory, relative to the project root. Leave it out for the project root itself. Macterm expands '~'. Absolute paths pass through unchanged. For a remote project, '~' and absolute paths are on the remote side (never the local home). In the pinned-tabs layout (path: <pinned>), each cwd is complete in itself: an absolute path, a path that is relative to '~', or a full [user@]host:dir spec.

run.description: The command that Macterm types into the shell of the pane when the pane starts (for example "npm run dev"). Leave it out for a plain shell. The command runs inside the shell, so the shell prompt stays when the command exits.

shell.description: The shell binary to start for this pane (for example "/bin/zsh"). Leave it out to use the shell from your Ghostty config (if none, your login shell).

pane.title: Pane (leaf)
pane.description: A terminal pane. With no fields ({}), it is a plain shell.

paneTab.title: Pane tab (leaf)
paneTab.description: A single-pane tab. With no pane fields, it is a plain shell.

direction.description: The direction of the split. 'horizontal' means side by side (first | second). 'vertical' means stacked (first / second).

ratio.description: The position of the divider, from 0 to 1. The default is 0.5 (an even split).

split.title: Split
split.description: Splits the area into two child nodes with a nested `split` mapping.

splitTab.title: Split tab
splitTab.description: A tab split into two child nodes.
